newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Alliance still examining shipper requests.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Alliance still examining shipper requests.

text.p: Canada's Alliance Pipeline, which earlier said it filed an application with the U.S. energy regulator, was still examining conditions submitted by prospective gas shippers in its autumn open season, a spokesman for the consortium said on Tuesday.

"We're obviously feeling pretty good about things but we did not submit a complete list of all the people that signed precedent agreements because, quite frankly, we are still finishing up with a couple," said Alliance vice-president Jack Crawford. "We did not want to release what we consider really to be competitive information."

In Alliance's precedent agreement, the pipeline consortium agreed to make regulatory filings and take the financial risks of building the massive natural gas line in exchange for shippers committing to sign up for 15 years of capacity if the line went ahead.

The C$3.6-billion producer-backed line, which would compete with such traditional pipeliners as NOVA Corp and TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, would ship 1.25 billion cubic feet of liquids-rich natural gas per day to Chicago from northeastern British Columbia.
Crawford said Alliance would likely make public the results of its open season, which was held for a month to gauge shipper support for the project, but a final decision had not been made.
Asked when disclosure of the results could occur, he said, "I'd prefer to keep those cards pretty close to my chest."
Alliance said on Tuesday it filed with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission its application for permission to build and operate the U.S. portion of the line.
It also said it informed Canada's National Energy Board it intended to make a similar application in Canada in Mid-1997. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
